title: Salt: the mineral that paid for empires
text: For most of history salt {{1}} so scarce and so necessary that it was worth fighting over, and governments quickly learned {{2}} taxing it was easier than mining it. Rome built the Via Salaria, {{3}} ran from the salt pans of the Adriatic straight to the capital, and emperors {{4}} revenues depended on the salt tax kept the price firmly under state control. The English word salary descends {{5}} the allowance once paid to Roman soldiers for the mineral, and whole wars were financed {{6}} this single levy. {{7}} 1930, Mahatma Gandhi chose the humble substance for his most famous protest, walking 240 miles to the sea to make salt from seawater in open defiance of the British salt laws, and the Salt March became a turning point {{8}} the long road to independence.

gaps.hint: verb: salt ___ so scarce and necessary
gaps.explanation: Past 'be' with an uncountable subject: was scarce.

gaps.hint: conjunction: learned ___ taxing it was easier
relative: the Via Salaria, ___ ran from
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the road.
'Whose' links the emperors to their revenues.
Origin of the word: descends from.

gaps.hint: preposition: wars were financed ___ this levy
gaps.explanation: Passive agent: financed by the levy.

gaps.hint: preposition: a turning point ___ the road
gaps.explanation: 'A turning point on the road' — position along the route takes 'on'.
